note: 나요. 생각이 나요 = it comes to mind; 냄새가 나요 = it smells.
웃어요. Regular (not ㅅ irregular).
기다려요. 잠깐만 기다려 주세요.
입어요. Regular (not ㅂ irregular). Hats: 쓰다; shoes: 신다.
끝나요. 수업이 끝났어요.
걸려요. 감기에 걸렸어요.
올라요. 르 irregular. 가격이 올랐어요.
믿어요. 저를 믿으세요.
바꿔요. 자리 바꿀까요? = shall we swap seats?
배워요. 한국어를 배워요.
도와요. ㅂ irregular (ㅂ → 오 here). Asking: 도와주세요.
이야기해요. Spoken: 얘기해요.
자요. To an elder: 주무세요.
걸어요. ㄷ irregular: ㄷ → ㄹ before a vowel.
울어요. ㄹ drops: 우세요, 우는 아이.

meaning: to get along; to spend days
note: 지내요. 잘 지냈어요? = how have you been?
팔아요. ㄹ drops: 파세요, 파는 곳.
태어나요. 서울에서 태어났어요.
가르쳐요. 영어를 가르쳐요.

meaning: to order (food); to make someone do
note: 시켜요. 치킨 시킬까요? = shall we order chicken?
원해요. Formal; day to day use -고 싶다.
잊어요. Spoken more: 잊어버리다.

meaning: to make an effort; to try hard
note: 노력해요. 더 노력할게요.
씻어요. 손 씻어요.
싸워요. 친구랑 싸웠어요.
전화해요. 이따 전화할게요 = I'll call you later.
준비해요. 준비됐어요? = are you ready?
결혼해요. 결혼했어요? = are you married?
찍어요. 사진 찍어 주세요.
도착해요. 몇 시에 도착해요?
빌려요. 책 빌려도 돼요? To lend: 빌려주다.
골라요. 르 irregular.
나아요. ㅅ irregular. 빨리 나으세요 = get well soon.
기억해요. 저 기억하세요? = do you remember me?
닫아요. Regular, unlike 듣다 / 걷다.
출발해요. 지금 출발해요.
켜요. 불 좀 켜 주세요 = turn the light on.
꺼요 (ㅡ drops). 핸드폰 꺼 주세요.
좋아져요. 날씨가 좋아졌어요.

meaning: to be the same; to be like
note: 같아요 · before a noun: 같은. 같은 반 = the same class.

meaning: to be so; to be like that
note: 그래요 · 그런 (ㅎ irregular). 그래요? = really?

meaning: to be how (what is it like?)
note: 어때요? · 어떤 (ㅎ irregular). 날씨 어때요?
이래요 · 이런 (ㅎ irregular). 왜 이래요? = what's wrong with you?
달라요 · 다른 (르 irregular).

meaning: to be new; to be fresh (feel new)
note: 새로워요 · 새로운 (ㅂ irregular). For things: 새 (new).
중요해요 · 중요한.
어려워요 · 어려운 (ㅂ irregular). 한국어 어려워요?
쉬워요 · 쉬운 (ㅂ irregular).
필요해요 · 필요한. 뭐가 필요해요? = what do you need?

meaning: to be high; to be tall (buildings)
note: 높아요 · 높은. People are 키가 커요, not 높아요.
길어요 · 긴 (ㄹ drops).
젊어요 · 젊은. Said [점따].
아파요 · 아픈 (ㅡ drops). 어디 아파요?

meaning: to be few; to be little
note: 적어요 · 적은. Opposite of 많다.
빨라요 · 빠른 (르 irregular).

meaning: to be wide; to be spacious
note: 넓어요 · 넓은. Said [널따].

meaning: to be strange; to be weird
note: 이상해요 · 이상한.
비슷해요 · 비슷한.
짧아요 · 짧은. Short people: 키가 작아요.
고마워요 · 고마운 (ㅂ irregular). Warmer, less formal than 감사합니다.
따뜻해요 · 따뜻한. Also for people: a warm person.
낮아요 · 낮은.

meaning: to be fun; to be enjoyable
note: 즐거워요 · 즐거운 (ㅂ irregular). 즐거운 주말 보내세요.

meaning: to be scary; to be scared
note: 무서워요 · 무서운 (ㅂ irregular).
가벼워요 · 가벼운 (ㅂ irregular).
건강해요 · 건강한.
밝아요 · 밝은. Said [박따]. Also: cheerful (a person).

meaning: to be comfortable; to be convenient
note: 편해요 · 편한.
깨끗해요 · 깨끗한.
어두워요 · 어두운 (ㅂ irregular).
미안해요 · 미안한. Formal apology: 죄송합니다.
유명해요 · 유명한.

meaning: to be glad; to be joyful
note: 기뻐요 · 기쁜 (ㅡ drops).
무거워요 · 무거운 (ㅂ irregular).
특별해요 · 특별한.
뜨거워요 · 뜨거운 (ㅂ irregular). Hot weather is 덥다.
친절해요 · 친절한. For staff, strangers.

meaning: to be narrow; to be cramped
note: 좁아요 · 좁은.

meaning: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient
note: 불편해요 · 불편한.

meaning: to be cool; to be refreshing
note: 시원해요 · 시원한. Also said of hot soup: "ah, that hits the spot".
반가워요 · 반가운 (ㅂ irregular).
차가워요 · 차가운 (ㅂ irregular). Cold weather is 춥다.
매워요 · 매운 (ㅂ irregular).
달아요 · 단 (ㄹ drops).
느려요 · 느린.
더러워요 · 더러운 (ㅂ irregular).
시끄러워요 · 시끄러운 (ㅂ irregular).
하얘요 · 하얀 (ㅎ irregular).
짜요 · 짠.
조용해요 · 조용한.
부러워요 · 부러운 (ㅂ irregular). 부러워요! = lucky you!
빨개요 · 빨간 (ㅎ irregular).
배불러요 · 배부른 (르 irregular).
재미없어요 · 재미없는 (있다/없다 take -는).
노래요 · 노란 (ㅎ irregular). 노래요 also = it's a song.
맛없어요 · 맛없는. Said [마덥따].
까매요 · 까만 (ㅎ irregular).
외로워요 · 외로운 (ㅂ irregular).
파래요 · 파란 (ㅎ irregular).

meaning: to be a hassle; can't be bothered
note: 귀찮아요 · 귀찮은. Very common in speech.
Right before the verb: 안 가요. With 하다 verbs: 공부 안 해요.
더 주세요 = more, please; 조금 더 = a bit more.
잘 자요 = sleep well; 잘 몰라요 = I don't really know.
또 봐요 = see you again; 또 늦었어요? = late again?
어떻게 가요? = how do I get there? 어떡해 = oh no (from 어떻게 해).
다시 한번 = once more.
다 먹었어요 = I ate it all; 다 왔어요 = we're almost there.
좀 도와주세요 sounds softer than 도와주세요. Short for 조금.
Everyday: 같이. 함께해요 = let's do it together.
많이 드세요 = eat plenty (said by a host).
가장 좋아하는 = my favorite. Spoken more: 제일.
바로 앞 = right in front; 바로 갈게요 = I'll come right away.
모두 같이 = all together.
왜요? = why? Sounds blunt alone; add 혹시 to soften.
특히 김치를 좋아해요.
아직 안 먹었어요 = I haven't eaten yet.
같이 가요 = let's go together. After a noun it is a particle: 꽃같이 = like a flower.
Right before the verb: 못 가요 = I can't go. 수영 못 해요.
너무 비싸요 = too expensive; 너무 좋아요 = I love it.
이미 끝났어요 = it's already over.
Neutral. Spoken more: 정말, 진짜, 너무.
그냥요 = no reason; 그냥 그래요 = so-so.
거의 다 왔어요 = almost there; 거의 안 먹어요 = I hardly eat.
곧 도착해요 = arriving soon.
서로 도와요 = we help each other.
정말 맛있어요. 정말요? = really?
혼자 왔어요 = I came alone.
이제 가요 = I'm going now; 이제 알겠어요 = now I get it.
꼭 오세요 = be sure to come.
요즘 바빠요?
계속 생각나요 = I keep thinking about it.
갑자기 비가 와요.
With a negative: 전혀 몰라요.
빨리 와요 = come quickly.
With comparisons: 훨씬 더 좋아요.
열심히 공부해요.
자주 와요? = do you come here often?
벌써 열 시예요? = it's ten already?
제일 좋아요 = it's the best.
Often with -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 아마 비가 올 거예요.
Spoken short form: 좀.
Spoken also: 늘, 언제나.
나중에 연락할게요.
With a negative: 별로 안 좋아해요. 별로예요 = it's meh.
가끔 만나요.
일찍 일어나요.
원래 그래요 = it's always like that.
늦게 자요 = I go to bed late.
보통 몇 시에 자요? Also a noun: regular size.
Softens a question: 혹시 한국 사람이에요?
Casual: 되게 맛있어. Not in writing.
금방 갈게요 = I'll be right there.
Stronger, more casual than 정말.
천천히 드세요 = take your time eating.
방금 왔어요 = I just got here.
To friends and younger people. With 가: 내가. My: 내.
Also "my" for family and home: 우리 엄마, 우리 집.

meaning: Mr. / Ms. (after a full or given name)
note: Names replace "you": 민수 씨, 어디 가요? Never after your own name or a surname alone.
Spoken: 그거. With 이: 그게.
The default with strangers. With 가: 제가. My: 제.
저 + 의. 제 이름은 … = my name is …
자신 있어요 = I'm confident. 자신을 사랑하세요.

meaning: you (casual, to a friend or a child)
note: Only to close friends or younger people. With 가: 네가 (said 니가).
뭐 해요? = what are you doing? Formal: 무엇.
누구예요? With 가: 누가 왔어요? = who came?
자기 일 = one's own business. 자기야 = honey.
무엇을 도와드릴까요? = how may I help you?
그거 좋네요 = that's a good one / good idea.
어디 가요? (often just a greeting: where are you off to?)
Spoken: 이거. With 이: 이게.
Rarely used face to face: it can sound cold or start a fight. Use the person's name or title instead.

meaning: there (near you, or the place we mentioned)
note: 거기 어디예요? = where is that place? Pairs with 여기 / 저기.
이거 얼마예요? Point and say 이거 주세요.
나 + 의. 내 친구 = my friend.
아무나 = anyone at all; 아무 때나 = any time.
아무도 없어요 = there's nobody here.
저거 뭐예요?
아무것도 몰라요 = I don't know anything.
뭔가 이상해요 = something's off.
To customers, elders, at work. It lowers your side, so it never includes the listener.
Addressing a group: 여러분, 안녕하세요!
누군가 왔어요 = someone came. Spoken: 누가.
Spoken: 저거. With 이: 저게.
Introducing someone: 이분은 김 선생님이세요.
From 이 아이. About a friend standing next to you: 얘는 제 친구예요.
이쪽으로 오세요 = come this way. 이쪽은 제 동생이에요.
From 그 아이. Common way to say "he/she" among friends.

meaning: you (to a stranger, lit. that side)
note: A way around saying 너 or 당신 to someone whose name you don't know. Can sound distant or a little cheeky.
저쪽에 있어요 = it's over there.
저분이 누구세요?
From 저 아이. Don't use it about elders.
어딘가에 있을 거예요 = it must be somewhere.
For someone respected: 그분이 오셨어요.
Speech uses the person's name or 그 사람, 걔. 그 also = that (before a noun).
Almost never spoken. Use the name, 그 사람 or 걔.
After a vowel or ㄹ: 로 (버스로, 지하철로); after a consonant: 으로 (손으로).
Same after vowels and consonants: 세 시까지, 서울까지.
아홉 시부터 = from nine. Pairs with 까지.
Makes a bare word polite: 저도요, 커피요, 왜요?
친구한테 줘요. Only for people and animals; places take 에.
Goes after the thing you compare against: 버스보다 빨라요 = faster than the bus.
친구들 = friends. Often left out: Korean doesn't need a plural.
Vowel: 랑 (친구랑); consonant: 이랑 (동생이랑). Spoken version of 하고.
Vowel: 나 (커피나 차); consonant: 이나 (빵이나 밥). 두 시간이나 = a whole two hours.
Same as 한테, a bit more formal: 선생님에게.
한국 사람처럼 말해요 = you talk like a Korean.
천 원밖에 없어요 = I only have 1,000 won. The verb must be negative.
세 시쯤 = around three; 얼마쯤 = about how much.
날마다 = every day; 주말마다 = every weekend.
Consonant: 아 (민정아); vowel: 야 (지수야). Only to friends and younger people.
Replaces 이/가 for elders: 할아버지께서 오셨어요.
Honorific 에게: 할머니께 드려요.
친구한테서 받았어요. Often shortened to 한테.
하나씩 = one each; 조금씩 = little by little.
커피라도 마실래요? = want to at least grab a coffee?
민수라고 해요 = I'm called Minsu.
마음대로 = as you like; 말한 대로 = as I said.
집에서부터 걸어왔어요 = I walked all the way from home.
-고 joins two actions or facts. Same after vowels and consonants: 가고, 먹고.
-아서/어서: one action leads to the next. 가서 먹어요 = I'll go there and eat.
-아서/어서 = because. Never with -(으)세요 or -(으)ㄹ까요.
Vowel stem: -면 (가면); consonant: -으면 (먹으면).
Sets the scene: 바쁜데 나중에 얘기해요. Verbs: 가는데; adjectives: 바쁜데.
-지만 = but. Same after any stem: 좋지만, 비싸지만.
Vowel: 갈 때; consonant: 먹을 때. 어릴 때 = when I was little.
-(으)니까 = because, and works with requests: 비가 오니까 우산 가져가세요.
비싸도 사고 싶어요.
한국에 가려고 한국어를 배워요.
Two things at once, same person: 음악 들으면서 걸어요.
Only with go / come: 먹으러 가요, 놀러 와요.
One action is interrupted: 집에 가다가 친구를 만났어요.
-거나 = or, between actions: 주말에 자거나 영화 봐요.
Vowel: 간 후에; consonant: 먹은 후에. Also -고 나서.
Verb + 기 전에: 먹기 전에 = before eating.
집에 도착하자마자 잤어요.
Books and news. In speech: 그런데, 하지만.
Written, formal.
The spoken short form of 그런데. Starts a new topic too: 근데 밥 먹었어?
Formal 그래서.
카드 또는 현금 = card or cash. Speech: 아니면, (이)나.
Also "exactly!": 그러니까요! Spoken short: 그니까.
Between 그런데 and 하지만 in tone.
A bit more formal than 그럼.
텔레비전을 봤어요. 그러다가 잠들었어요.
비싸요. 게다가 맛도 없어요.
The all-purpose reaction: 아, 그래요? Also a sigh.
Surprise or a casual "yeah": 어, 왔어? Casual.
Neutral, anyone can say it. Longer = more impressed: 와아.
Pleasantly surprised: 오, 멋있다! Also spelled like 오 (five).
Casual "yes" to friends. To elders: 네.
Getting started or handing something over: 자, 시작할까요?
Thinking before you answer. Fine in any register.
Bigger, more childlike than 와.
Only on the phone, or to check if someone hears you. Not a greeting in person.
Polite: 글쎄요. Buys time or softens a "no".
Light disbelief or teasing: 에이, 거짓말! Casual.

meaning: oh my god (lit. in the world)
note: Amazement or shock. Common with older speakers: 세상에, 이게 뭐야!
Relief. Also a sigh.
Sudden pain. Shorter: 아! Children say 아야야.
Tired resignation. Can sound grumpy; be careful with elders.
Mostly women and older speakers. 어머나 is stronger.
Shock, also typed in chats. Casual.
Sudden small surprise or mistake. Casual.
When you remember a mistake: 아차, 지갑! Casual.
When startled. Casual; polite: 깜짝 놀랐어요.
Shy or mildly annoyed, often playful. Usually women.
Small personal victory. Also written 앗싸. Casual, a bit playful.
Asking for quiet. Anyone can say it.
A scream: a bug, a fright, a disaster. Casual.
Showing off a surprise or a gift. Playful.
Disgust, especially at food. Casual; rude to say about someone's cooking.

meaning: this / that / that (over there) (before a noun)
note: 이 사람, 그 책, 저 건물. 그 = near you or already mentioned; 저 = far from both.

meaning: one, two, three, four (before a counter)
note: 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네: 한 잔, 두 명.

meaning: this kind of / that kind of / that kind of (over there)
note: 이런 날 = a day like this. 그런 거 아니에요 = it's not like that.

meaning: what kind of; some (before a noun)
note: 어떤 음식 좋아해요? From 어떻다.
다른 거 있어요? = do you have another one?
여러 번 = many times; 여러 가지 = all sorts.
어느 나라 = which country; 어느 쪽 = which way.
모든 사람 = everyone.
이번 주말 = this weekend; 이번이 처음이에요.
몇 개? = how many? 몇 명 = a few people.
무슨 일 있어요? = is something wrong?
지난 주말 = last weekend; 지난달 = last month.
새 옷 = new clothes; 새해 = New Year.
Agreeing: 네, 맞아요. Casual: 맞아.
More formal than 네; heard in offices and from older people.
오후 세 시 = 3 p.m.
첫눈 = the first snow; 첫 데이트 = a first date.
올해 몇 살이에요?
To friends. Also starts a protest: 아니, 그게 아니라…
영 in maths and scores; 공 in phone numbers: 공일공 = 010.
Also 지난해.
To friends and children, both hello and goodbye.
낮에는 더워요 = it's hot during the day.
오전 열 시 = 10 a.m.
새벽 두 시 = 2 a.m.
One word, no space.
Short form of 아니요; softer and more common in speech.
스물 → 스무: 스무 살 = twenty years old.
화 = fire. 월화수목금토일.
수 = water.
목 = wood.
Before a counter: 스무.
내년에 한국에 가요.
Mostly for age: 서른 살. Sino-Korean 삼십 is used for money and minutes.
백 원; 이백 = 200. Not 일백.
열 + 하나: 열한 시 = 11 o'clock.
내일모레 = in a couple of days.
Also 그제.
대 counts vehicles and machines: 차 두 대, 컴퓨터 한 대.
분 is the polite 명: 몇 분이세요? = how many in your party?
벌 counts sets of clothes: 옷 한 벌.
장미 한 송이 = one rose.
김밥 한 줄 = one gimbap roll; 한 줄로 = in a line.
만두 한 접시 = a plate of dumplings.
피자 한 조각, 케이크 한 조각.
한 가지 더 = one more thing; 여러 가지 = all kinds.
두 군데 = two places. Spoken, everyday.
노래 한 곡 = one song (at karaoke).
영화 한 편 봐요 = we watch a movie.

meaning: one pill; one small round thing
note: 약 한 알 = one pill.
맥주 한 캔 = a can of beer.

meaning: one game; one round; one tray
note: 게임 한 판 = one round; 계란 한 판 = a tray of 30 eggs.
Hours use native numbers: 한 시, 두 시 … 열두 시.
Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers: 오 분, 십 분, 삼십 분.
Years use Sino-Korean: 일 년, 이 년. Native: 한 해.
Sino-Korean months: 삼 개월. Native: 석 달.
Korean BBQ is ordered by portion: 삼겹살 이 인분 = pork belly for two.
번째 makes ordinals: 두 번째 = second, 세 번째 = third.
예뻐요. Mostly to women, also to kids and things. Mild; everyone hears it. No gender forms in Korean.
귀여워요 (ㅂ irregular). To anyone, men included. Mild and playful.
Said in the past tense: 잘생겼어요. Mostly to men. Warm.
아름다워요 (ㅂ irregular). Strong and a bit poetic: for scenery, or a very sincere compliment. Bold.
사랑스러워요 (ㅂ irregular). Tender, more for couples. Warm.
매력 있어요 = you're attractive. Safe and common. Mild to warm.
매력적이에요. A notch more serious than 매력 있어요. Warm.
똑똑해요. To anyone. Mild. To an elder, praise their knowledge instead.
착해요. Big compliment from a partner's family; to equals or juniors only. Mild.

meaning: to be affectionate; sweet and caring
note: 다정해요. A top quality in a partner. Warm.
미소가 예뻐요. A little literary; speech also uses 웃는 모습. Mild.
눈이 예뻐요. Praising eyes is safe and common. (눈 also = snow.) Mild to warm.
A Korean favourite: eyes curving into crescents when you smile. Warm.
보조개가 귀여워요. A classic Korean compliment. Mild.
목소리가 좋아요. Safe, very common, especially on the phone. Mild.
웃음이 많아요 = you laugh a lot (a good thing). Mild.
분위기 있어요 = you have a certain charm. Very Korean compliment. Warm.
제 스타일이에요 = you're my type. Mild alone; warm in that phrase.
성격 좋아요 is high praise. Mild.
센스 있어요 = you've got taste / you're thoughtful. Mild.
Koreans ask 이상형이 뭐예요? on first dates and in interviews. Mild as a question.
첫인상이 좋았어요 = I liked you from the start. Warm.
Slang, from 훈훈한 남자. For women: 훈녀. Mild, friendly.
Slang: 심장이 쿵. 심쿵했어요 = you made my heart skip. Warm, playful.
To a woman you know. 오늘따라 = today especially. Warm.
Right after learning a name. Mild, sweet.

meaning: You must hear that you're pretty a lot
note: Indirect and smooth. To a woman. Warm.
Teasing, to anyone. Warm.
To someone you know well. 짓 = little actions. Warm, playful.
Polite -시-; to a man you don't know well. Mild to warm.
After seeing photos first (dating app, a friend's phone). Warm.
To anyone dressed up. Mild.

meaning: You look cool when you're working
note: Classic office or café crush line. Warm.
To someone your age or younger. Mild.
Safe on a date or between friends. Mild to warm.
Polite and playful. Warm.
Safe on a first meeting. Mild.

meaning: Your eye smile is really pretty
note: Very Korean compliment. Warm.
Mild, sweet.

meaning: You have a really nice voice
note: Often on the phone or after karaoke. Mild.

meaning: I wanted to hear your voice
note: Why you called. To someone you're dating. Warm to bold.

meaning: You have a certain charm about you
note: A refined compliment to men or women. Warm.
Mild; works with near-strangers.
Light and direct. Warm.
Bold and playful. Usually after a few dates.
The classic first-date question. Mild.

meaning: I liked my first impression of you
note: On a second date. Warm.

meaning: And you have a great personality too
note: 도 = on top of being good-looking. Warm.
After a kind gesture. Warm.

meaning: Have you eaten? (I care about you)
note: Korean's indirect "I'm thinking of you". Polite form of the casual 밥 먹었어? Mild.
Often polite filler; when meant, it opens a date. Ask "when?" to show you mean it. Mild.
The real invitation. Warm.
Easy opener after class or work. Mild.

meaning: Is it OK if I contact you?
note: Polite way to ask for KakaoTalk. Mild.
At the end of a first meeting. Warm.

meaning: Want to come up for some ramyeon? (joke line)
note: From the film One Fine Spring Day (2001), where the line is 라면 먹을래요?; this meme version means an invitation inside. Joke only, never a real move.
Playful deflection, shy but not a no. Casual and friendly.
Teasing deflection; smiling = interested, flat = not. Mild.
A warm yes to an invitation.

meaning: Thanks for the thought, but I'm fine
note: Kind, clear no. Works for a drink or a number.
Clear no; nobody will push after this.

meaning: You're a lovely person, but I'd like to stay friends
note: Gentle no to someone you know. 분 keeps it respectful.

meaning: I'm not looking to date right now
note: Firm but not personal.
-네요 = noticing out loud. Say it to the host or cook during the meal.
솜씨 = skill with your hands. Polite -시-; fine to elders.
Asking for the recipe is praise in itself.
For any skill. To elders, praise with -시- and no grading words.
To colleagues and friends. To a boss: 좋은 생각이신 것 같아요.
A big compliment at work.
To equals or juniors. It sounds odd said to a much older person.

meaning: You have a great sense of humor
note: Polite; to anyone.
배려 = thinking of others. Highly valued.
Always busy and on time. Different from 열심히 하시네요 (works hard at it).
A very common, friendly compliment in Korea, to men and women alike.

meaning: You look so young for your age
note: A favorite compliment, especially to people over 30.
Literally "your impression is good". Said on first meeting.
Said on a first visit, often with a gift (휴지, fruit).
Parents will usually deflect: 아니에요, 말썽꾸러기예요.
A compliment to the parents too. Very welcome.
Literally "the photo came out well".
Polite -세요; to anyone, including elders.
What learners hear right after 한국어 잘하시네요.
Friendly exaggeration to a learner.
Usually follows the compliment; itself a compliment.
To a friend or junior. To an elder it sounds like grading.
The polite way to praise a boss: you report your experience, you don't grade them.
The safest praise for a senior, teacher or boss.

meaning: Thank you for all your hard work
note: Praises effort. Fine among colleagues; some seniors find 수고 from a junior presumptuous, so to a boss 감사합니다 is safer.
The first reflex after any compliment: deflect, even if you're pleased.

meaning: Oh no, I still have a long way to go
note: The standard modest reply, especially about your Korean.

meaning: Don't mention it; you're too kind
note: Polite and a little formal. To elders and at work.
Literally "that's too much praise". Polite, a bit formal.
Accepting warmly. More common among younger people.

meaning: Thanks for seeing it that way
note: Modest and grateful at once.
The host's answer to praise for food or a gift.
Turns the praise back onto the other person. Warm and humble.
한국 is everyday speech; the official name is 대한민국. 한국 사람 = Korean (person); 한국어 or 한국말 = Korean.
South Korean usage. The official name is 조선민주주의인민공화국.

중국 사람 = Chinese (person); 중국어 = Chinese.

홍콩 사람. 광둥어 = Cantonese.
몽골 사람; 몽골어 = Mongolian.
러시아 사람; 러시아어 = Russian.

인도 사람; 힌디어 = Hindi.

브라질 사람. People speak 포르투갈어.
멕시코 사람. People speak 스페인어.
필리핀 사람 = Filipino (person); 필리핀어 or 타갈로그어 = Filipino, Tagalog.
베트남 사람; 베트남어 = Vietnamese.
영국 사람 = British (person); 영어 = English (irregular: not 영국어).
캐나다 사람. People speak 영어 and 프랑스어.
호주 사람 = Australian. 호주 is from the Chinese characters; 오스트레일리아 is also correct.
독일 사람; 독일어 = German.
프랑스 사람; 프랑스어 = French.
스페인 사람; 스페인어 = Spanish.
이탈리아 사람; 이탈리아어 = Italian.
태국 사람; 태국어 = Thai.
The official Korean name since 2022; the older 터키 is still common. 튀르키예어 = Turkish.
아랍어 = Arabic.
The country. The US state is also 조지아.
Not the island country Dominica (도미니카 연방).
One of the four nations of the United Kingdom (영국).
포르투갈 사람; 포르투갈어 = Portuguese.
네덜란드 사람; 네덜란드어 = Dutch.
폴란드 사람; 폴란드어 = Polish.
우크라이나 사람; 우크라이나어 = Ukrainian.
